Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you know, I'm Marisol, the HR Director, and I'll be facilitating this case review regarding the complaint filed by Iris related to several disagreements with Ken that became visible during team meetings. These disagreements involved public corrections, disputed ownership of follow-up tasks, and tense exchanges in front of colleagues.

My standard process for this type of review is to give each participant a turn to state their relevant observations, concerns, and any policy requirements they believe apply. I'll be recording everything shared before I make my decision on the case finding and any corrective working arrangement.

Before we begin, I want to set a few ground rules: please speak one at a time, focus on facts and observations rather than characterizations, and be respectful of each other's perspectives. My goal is to understand the full picture so I can reach a fair and well-informed decision.

Iris, would you like to begin by sharing your observations and concerns?

transcript.text:
Thank you, Marisol. I appreciate the opportunity to share my perspective. I want to be factual about what I've observed and experienced.

Over the past several weeks, there have been multiple instances during team meetings where Ken has publicly corrected me on points that were either matters of interpretation or that I had already addressed. On at least two occasions, there were disputes about who was responsible for follow-up tasks that had been assigned to me, with Ken asserting ownership in ways that undermined my role in front of colleagues. The exchanges that followed were tense and uncomfortable, not just for me and Ken, but for everyone in the room.

These incidents have affected my ability to collaborate effectively and have created an environment where I feel hesitant to contribute in meetings. I filed the complaint because I believe these patterns need to be addressed formally so that we can establish a clear and respectful working arrangement going forward.

I do have a specific request regarding corrective arrangements, but I'd like to share that when we get to the discussion of potential solutions, if that's appropriate.

decisions.finding: The complaint is substantiated. The record establishes multiple incidents of public corrections, disputed task ownership, and tense exchanges during team meetings. Ken's own observations confirm four incidents stemming from an undocumented handoff process, which, while not characterized as intentional disrespect, resulted in a pattern of public corrections and role undermining that adversely affected Iris's working environment. The corrective working arrangement will address both the process gap and the interpersonal dynamic.

commitments.detail: A written outcome documenting the case finding and corrective arrangement will be issued within 10 business days, per the policy requirement confirmed by Darius.
A separate private support meeting with Iris will be scheduled, distinct from the written outcome, as required by policy.
No direct one-to-one meetings between Iris and Ken for 30 days. A weekly mediated check-in will be held instead to facilitate collaboration and monitor the working relationship.
Ken will work with the team to document the handoff process for follow-up tasks to prevent future ambiguity in task ownership and reduce the likelihood of public disputes.
